China's Military 
April 26, 2026

The PLA enters May 2026 in an unusual posture... extraordinary external activity layered on top of an internal leadership crisis without modern precedent. 

Active operations cluster around three flashpoints simultaneously (Taiwan Strait, waters east of Luzon, and the Senkaku/East China Sea corridor), all timed to counter the trilateral U.S.-Japan-Philippines convergence that crystallized at Balikatan 2026 (April 20–May 8). 

Internally, the Central Military Commission has been hollowed out to two functioning members (Xi and Zhang Shengmin) following the January 2026 purge of CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia and Joint Staff Chief Liu Zhenli, with 36 senior officers stripped of NPC delegate status since the 20th Party Congress. 

Fujian carrier closing on full operational capability, nuclear stockpile past 600 warheads on track to double, Pentagon-confirmed PLA delivery of 12 submarines, 1 carrier, 2 cruisers, 10 destroyers, and 7 frigates since 2024. 

The U.S. opportunity vacuum is the variable to watch closely… three U.S. carrier strike groups are forward-deployed to the Middle East for the Iran blockade, leaving USS George Washington (in port in Yokosuka) as the sole U.S. flattop in INDOPACOM AOR.

Leadership Signals

This is the most consequential development of the quarter and the section most underweighted in mainstream coverage.

CMC reduced to two functioning members. Following the January 2026 removal of Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia (the second-most powerful military leader in China) and the apparent ouster of Joint Staff Chief Liu Zhenli, the seven-member Central Military Commission now has only Xi Jinping and Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin (anti-corruption portfolio) actively functioning.

Cumulative purge data: Since the 20th Party Congress (October 2022), 36 senior officers have been publicly stripped of NPC delegate status, including 16 full generals, 14 lieutenant generals, and 6 major generals. Nearly all 16 purged full generals were personally promoted by Xi. The roster includes former CMC Vice Chairman He Weidong, former CMC Political Work Department head Miao Hua, former Defense Minister Li Shangfu, former Rocket Force commanders Zhou Yaning and Li Yuchao, former Air Force commander Ding Laihang, former Navy commander Shen Jinlong, and former Navy political commissar Yuan Huazhi.

Xi's March 7, 2026 NPC speech: "The military carries guns. There absolutely cannot be anyone in the military who harbors disloyalty to the Party, and there absolutely cannot be any place for corrupt elements to hide." The speech telegraphed continuing purges through the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030).

Xi's April 8, 2026 NDU speech to senior officers stressed political rectification ahead of the August 2027 PLA centenary. Xi linked the centenary goal to PLA's ability to "win local wars" in his 2022 work report.

2026 defense budget: +6.9% from 2025 actual spending. Note this is below recent years' announced growth rates, possibly reflecting fiscal pressure or political reorganization absorbing managerial bandwidth.

Active Operations & Deployments

PLA Eastern Theater Command, Vessel Formation 133... On April 19, 2026, Type 052D destroyer Baotou (Hull 133) led a formation through the Yokoate Waterway into the Western Pacific for "routine training," explicitly framed by Global Times as a deterrent message timed two days after a Japanese destroyer transited the Taiwan Strait on April 17. The formation completed its training and returned through the Yonaguni-Iriomote Waterway around April 25.

PLA Southern Theater Command, Task Force 107... Conducted live-fire, sea-air coordination, and underway replenishment drills east of Luzon Island, Philippines, announced April 24, explicitly as response to Balikatan 2026. This is the highest-profile PLA Southern Theater operation of the month and directly overlaps the Balikatan window.

PLA Navy 77th Anniversary... April 23 open-ship events in 10+ cities (Dalian, Qingdao, Shanghai, Ningbo, Xiamen, Guangzhou, Sanya, others) with 40+ active-duty vessels publicly displayed. Both scale and variety set records. A delegation of Taiwan visitors attended in Qingdao, included in PRC propaganda framing as cross-strait "compatriot" engagement... PRC state media only on the political framing.

Taiwan ADIZ tempo... As of April 26, 2026... 28 PLA aircraft sorties and 8 PLAN ships around Taiwan, with 18 of 28 sorties crossing the median line into northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ. Sustained high tempo continuing the 2024–2025 trend.. 3,615 sorties in 2024, 4,000+ from January–September 2025.

Taiwan Strait Situation

The structural baseline shifted decisively at the close of 2025. Justice Mission 2025 (December 29–30) was the first major PLA exercise to push Chinese military and Coast Guard vessels in significant numbers (11 PLAN vessels, 8 CCG vessels) into Taiwan's 12-nautical-mile contiguous zone, the buffer Beijing had largely respected for decades. The Diplomat assessed this as a normalization step rather than a one-time event, lowering thresholds for future operations.

A puzzling two-week pause in PLA aircraft activity around Taiwan occurred in early March 2026, the longest gap since Taiwan began publicly releasing daily data. PLATracker founder Ben Lewis tied the pause most plausibly to the planned (now rescheduled) Xi-Trump meeting. Activity resumed March 12.

President Lai Ching-te has publicly committed Taiwan to 5% of GDP defense spending by 2030.

South China Sea & Maritime Theater

Balikatan 2026 (April 20–May 8) is the inflection point of the spring quarter. Japan participates as a "full active participant" with combat-capable troops on Philippine soil for the first time since WWII, building on the September 2025 Japan-Philippines Reciprocal Access Agreement and the January 2026 ACSA. More than a dozen partner nations are participating.

Scarborough Shoal: Reuters-obtained satellite imagery from April 10–11 shows China deploying fishing boats, a naval/coast guard vessel, and a new floating barrier across the entrance, with Manila pushing its own vessels to protect Filipino fishermen.

Pagasa/Thitu Island: Philippines unveiled its first dedicated Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group command on April 9, covering 68,000 square kilometers, with multiple Chinese Coast Guard vessels visibly patrolling outlying waters during the unveiling ceremony.

Weapons & Capability Developments

Fujian (CV-18)... Commissioned November 5, 2025 at Yulin Naval Base, Sanya. State media announced April 19 that 2026 is the year of full transition from initial to full combat capability, with first far-sea Western Pacific training expected. April 5 satellite imagery showed Fujian operating in the Bohai Sea near Qinhuangdao with at least one escort. The carrier integrates J-35 stealth fighters, J-15T multirole fighters, J-15DT electronic warfare variants, and KJ-600 AEW&C aircraft via electromagnetic catapult, making Fujian the world's first carrier to launch a fifth-generation fighter via EMALS. Fourth carrier (likely nuclear-powered Type 004) reportedly under construction at Dalian.

Type 055 destroyers... Two newly commissioned Renhai-class destroyers assigned to Eastern Theater Command Navy (March 2026), framed in PRC media as cross-strait deterrence platforms.

Nuclear forces (PLARF)... Pentagon estimate: 600+ warheads, projected to "more than double" within five years per Paparo's April 21 testimony. Federation of American Scientists tracks ~462 launchers capable of reaching CONUS. Three solid-fuel silo fields (Yumen, Hami, Ordos) with ~350 silos. DF-5C liquid-fuel ICBM with multi-megaton warhead unveiled at the September 2025 parade, expanding from 18 to 48 DF-5 silos. DF-61 road-mobile ICBM with up to 12 MIRVs allows rapid warhead surge. JL-1 air-launched ballistic missile now operational on H-6N. Type 096 SSBN with JL-3 in development. New START lapsed February 2026 removing all bilateral arms control constraints.

PLARF readiness anomalies... A March 2026 Air University CASI report ("Dancers at the Knife's Edge") catalogs vulnerabilities... warhead stockpile heavily concentrated at Hongchuan/Base 67 in Baoji with single-road-access risk, outdated computer systems vulnerable to "left of launch" cyber, ongoing recruitment problems for skilled nuclear managers, no corresponding growth in nuclear support units despite warhead doubling.

2026 National Defense Strategy... "Deter China through strength, not confrontation," with emphasis on no country becoming a regional hegemon. $300M+ in EDCA infrastructure investments in the Philippines committed to date.

Foreign Assessments

Japan... Prime Minister Takaichi's November 2025 statement that Japan's military could intervene if China takes action against Taiwan triggered the ongoing China-Japan diplomatic crisis. 

Tokyo deployed upgraded Type-12 surface-to-ship missiles (1,000 km range) at Camp Kengun, Kumamoto, on March 31, 2026, putting much of China's east coast and the East China Sea within range. Hyper Velocity Gliding Projectile (HVGP) deployed at Camp Fuji simultaneously. 

Tokyo establishing a new Pacific Defense Office (April 2026 announcement) specifically to address PLA Pacific operations. Japan's FY2026 defense budget +9.4% with 2% GDP target hit by March 2026, two years ahead of schedule. Japan agreed to purchase 400 Tomahawks (1,600 km range), with JS Chokai Aegis destroyer configured for Tomahawk launch.

U.S. Intelligence Community 2026 Annual Threat Assessment... Assessed that China does not plan to invade Taiwan in 2027. This is significant because 2027 (PLA centenary, Xi's stated readiness benchmark) had been the operative planning horizon. The assessment shifts probable conflict windows later, while preserving the structural threat trajectory.

Escalation Watch

The four indicators most worth tracking over the next 30–60 days, ranked...

1. U.S. Indo-Pacific carrier vacuum. Three U.S. CSGs in CENTCOM (Ford in Red Sea, Lincoln in Arabian Sea, Bush newly arrived 5th Fleet), Eisenhower just out of 15-month maintenance, Vinson in maintenance, Roosevelt in 3rd Fleet AOR, Nimitz off Chile. George Washington (Yokosuka) is the sole U.S. carrier in INDOPACOM AOR and is in port. This is the most significant force-posture vulnerability in the Pacific in years, and historically the PLA has used U.S. distraction windows to advance gray-zone positions. Watch for unannounced Fujian or Shandong far-sea deployments, contiguous-zone breaches, or Scarborough Shoal escalation while U.S. attention remains in the Gulf.

2. PLA leadership decapitation effects on operational planning. A CMC reduced to two functional members during a period of multi-theater operational tempo creates two opposing risks... paralysis (cautious, defensive posture as new leaders consolidate) or unsupervised escalation (theater commanders making decisions without clear higher-level review). Watch for command friction signals... contradictory PRC statements, unexplained pauses, theater-specific actions inconsistent with central messaging. The early March ADIZ pause may have been an early example.

3. Japan-Philippines axis hardening. Marcos state visit to Japan May 26–29 will likely produce additional security agreements. The Japan-Philippines convergence is doing real strategic work that the Philippines or Japan alone could not do, and Beijing's reaction has been operationally serious (Task Force 107, Yokoate transit). The PLA's Eastern Theater Command spokesperson April 19 statement that China "will leave no strategic ambiguity for any military intervention in the Taiwan Straits" is a direct warning to Tokyo.

4. Nuclear posture inflection. New START lapsed February 2026 with no replacement framework. Pentagon assessment that Beijing "probably would consider nuclear first use if a conventional military defeat in Taiwan gravely threatened regime survival" sits in tension with China's official no-first-use policy reaffirmed in the November 2025 Arms Control White Paper. The DF-61's 12-MIRV capacity allows rapid warhead surge. Watch for additional warhead production indicators, silo activations across the three solid-fuel fields, and Type 096 SSBN program milestones.
